title: Salisbury steak
subtitle: Beef patties in a savoury mushroom and onion gravy
excerpt: Salisbury steak is a seasoned beef patty fried until browned on both sides, then finished in a thick mushroom and onion gravy until cooked through. Named after a nineteenth-century American doctor, it became a fixture of school cafeterias and TV dinners. Made well, it is a satisfying weeknight plate.
sourceNotes: American culinary tradition. Named after Dr James Salisbury, who promoted a ground-beef-centred diet in the 1880s. The dish became popular in the mid-twentieth century, appearing in Joy of Cooking and as a staple of American TV dinner culture.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked patties in the gravy for up to 2 months.

content.text: Salisbury steak is a flat oval beef patty seasoned with Worcestershire, onion, and breadcrumbs, pan-fried until browned, then finished in a mushroom and beef-stock gravy. The patties are denser than a burger because they are meant to cook through in the sauce. Served over mashed potato or egg noodles, it feeds four from 500 g of beef mince.

Mix {{beef-mince}} of beef mince with {{breadcrumbs-dried}} of dried breadcrumbs, the beaten egg, {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce, {{onion-powder}} of onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Form into 4 oval patties about 1.5 cm thick. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the patties for 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in the same pan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add {{chestnut-mushrooms}} of mushrooms and {{garlic}} of garlic. Cook for 3 minutes. Sprinkle over the gravy {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir for 1 minute. Pour in {{stock-beef}} of beef stock and {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Stir until smooth.
Return the patties to the pan. Simmer covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the patties are cooked through and the gravy has thickened. Serve over mashed potato.

items.cause: Not enough binder or patties flipped too soon.
items.fix: Ensure the egg and breadcrumbs are properly incorporated. Wait until the patties release naturally before flipping.

items.cause: Flour added directly to the liquid without cooking first.
items.fix: Cook the flour in the butter for 1 minute before adding the stock.

content.text: French-onion Salisbury steak uses caramelised onions and beef stock only, no mushrooms, and is finished with a slice of Swiss cheese melted on top. Serve over egg noodles for a simpler weeknight version.

Salisbury steak sits in a specific corner of American food culture: the TV dinner, the school cafeteria, the mid-century comfort meal. Its reputation as institutional food is not fully deserved. Made with good beef mince and a properly seasoned gravy, it is a satisfying weeknight dinner.
